chapter: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
title: Writing for Sarah Vaughan; two pianos; Jerry Valentine
summary: Hines stages Vaughan at a second piano, Budd becomes her chief arranger alongside Jerry Valentine.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Earl was a great show business man. He was looking for the flash. And Sarah Vaughan, she came with the band, and I started to writing music for her.
About what year was that, Budd?
This was in -- now let me try to be exact. This had to be --
(Unintelligible), because I'm sure it's a matter of record, because (you just went) off the cutt. Right.
Yeah. Now let me think. This had to be between '40 and '41. See?
Uh-huh. Well, she sang and she played, and she was like -- I remember this very distinctly.

Yes, in fact, Earl's got -- Billy Eckstine's got pictures of her. Unfortunately, I don't have any. But she and Earl sitting at the piano at the Appolo stage when we came back. She was then, later, playing the piano, and they had two pianos put on the stage.
And you wrote some of those arrangements for them, huh, Budd?
Oh, yeah, well, I was like the chief arranger at that time. We also had another very good arranger in the band named Jerry Valentine at that time.
He played trombone and piano. In fact, when he left Earl's band, he was the first piano to go out with Billy Eckstine, and when Billy left Earl's band.
